title: IN OEA 2025 OALP 109: Town of Grabill, 2025 OALP 109
text:
ISSUED:
STATE OF INDIANA
December 30, 2025 OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW PROCEEDINGS
DAVID COLE,
Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner, Administra(cid:415)ve Case Number: IDEM-2502-000857
v. Agency Ac(cid:415)on: Page Road Sanitary Extension,
Permit Approval No. 25694
TOWN OF GRABILL,
Permi(cid:425)ee/Respondent,
and
INDIANA DEPARTMENT OF
ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
Respondent.
FINAL ORDER GRANTING SUMMARY JUDGMENT
The Administra(cid:415)ve Law Judge (“ALJ”) Vanessa Voigt Gould, having reviewed the record
and the pleadings filed by the par(cid:415)es on Summary Judgment, now issues this Final Order as it
relates to the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for Administra(cid:415)ve Review filed by David Cole (“Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner”) on the 327 IAC
3 Construc(cid:415)on Permit, Page Road Sanitary Extension, Permit Approval No. 25694, issued to the
Town of Grabill (“Town”) by the Indiana Department of Environmental Management (“IDEM”) on
February 10, 2025. This decision is favorable to the Town and the IDEM (referred to collec(cid:415)vely
below as “Respondents”). Any aggrieved party may appeal this decision. Appeal instruc(cid:415)ons are
at the end of this document.
Jurisdic(cid:415)on
The ALJ assigned to this proceeding by the Director of the Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law
Proceedings (“OALP”), see Ind. Code § 4-15-10.5-13, has jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case pursuant to
Indiana Code § 4-15-10.5-12, which gives the OALP jurisdic(cid:415)on over agency administra(cid:415)ve ac(cid:415)ons
subject to the Indiana Administra(cid:415)ve Orders and Procedures Act at Indiana Code Art. 4-21.5
(“AOPA”) or “any other statute that requires or allows the office to take ac(cid:415)on.” The OALP has
jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case because this case is governed by AOPA.
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No.: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689 1 of 11

Issue
Whether, based on the undisputed material facts in the recod, the Respondents are
en(cid:415)tled to judgment as a ma(cid:425)er of law on the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for Review filed by the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner seeking
administra(cid:415)ve review of the 327 IAC 3 Construc(cid:415)on Permit, Page Road Sanitary Extension, Permit
Approval No. 25694 (the “Permit”), issued to the Town by the IDEM on February 10, 2025.
Procedural History
1. On February 10, 2025, IDEM issued an Authoriza(cid:415)on for Construc(cid:415)on of Sanitary Sewer
System Under 327 IAC 3, Permit Approval No. 25694 (the “Permit”).
2. A pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for administra(cid:415)ve review of the Permit was filed by Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner with the OALP on
February 28, 2025.
3. The OALP assigned ALJ Lori Kyle Endris to preside over this ma(cid:425)er that same day.
4. ALJ Endris issued a No(cid:415)ce of Insufficient Filing (“NOI”) on March 3, 2025.
5. On March 6, 2025, this ma(cid:425)er was reassigned to ALJ Vanessa Voigt Gould and an Order
was issued affirming the NOI.
6. On April 7, 2025, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner supplemented and/or amended his Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for Review.
7. An Ini(cid:415)al Prehearing Conference was held in this ma(cid:425)er on April 24, 2025.
8. On August 25, 2025, the Respondents filed a Joint Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment and
Memorandum of Law in Support of their Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment which included
the designa(cid:415)on of one exhibit, Respondents’ Exhibit A, the Permit Applica(cid:415)on Package for
Permit Approval 25694, VCF #83763768 (56 pages).
9. On September 24, 2025, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner filed a Response to Summary Judgment and counter
designa(cid:415)on of evidence. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s counter designa(cid:415)on of evidence was nearly iden(cid:415)cal
to Respondents’ Exhibit A referenced above, however, it varied in that Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner had
added comments and/or notes to the document.
10. On October 9, 2025, the Respondents filed a Reply in Support of their Mo(cid:415)on for Summary
Judgment and the record on summary judgment closed.
FINDINGS OF FACT
The following are undisputed material facts:
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 2 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

1. On November 5, 2024, the Town submi(cid:425)ed an applica(cid:415)on for a construc(cid:415)on permit to the
IDEM proposing to build a low-pressure sanitary sewer system (Respondents’ Exhibit A to
Respondents’ Brief in Support of Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment (“Respondents’ Exhibit
A”), pp. 10-22).
2. The applica(cid:415)on sought to extend an exis(cid:415)ng sanitary sewer system along Page Road in the
Town of Grabill, Indiana (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 2).
3. The Town supplemented its applica(cid:415)on on December 2, 2024, through the submission of
plans and specifica(cid:415)ons that were prepared by DLZ Indiana, LLC and cer(cid:415)fied by Casey
Erwin, Professional Engineer (Respondents’ Exhibit A, pp. 2, 23-25).
4. The Town later supplied addi(cid:415)onal informa(cid:415)on to the IDEM and submi(cid:425)ed a revised
applica(cid:415)on on February 3, 2025 (Respondents’ Exhibit A, pp. 2, 26-56).
5. On February 10, 2025, IDEM issued an Authoriza(cid:415)on for Construc(cid:415)on of Sanitary Sewer
System Under 327 IAC 3, Permit Approval No. 25694 (the “Permit”) (Respondents’ Exhibit
A, pp. 2-9).
6. The Permit authorizes the construc(cid:415)on of a low-pressure sanitary sewer system along
Page Road extending approximately 3,665 feet south from the intersec(cid:415)on with Witmer
Road and along Witmer Road extending approximately 431 feet east from the intersec(cid:415)on
with Page Road (the “Project”) (Respondents’ Exhibit A, pp. 2 and 5).
7. The Project involves the installa(cid:415)on of approximately 56 feet of 10-inch diameter PVC
(ASTM D3034 SDR-35) sanitary sewer and approximately 4,105 feet of 3-inch small
diameter HDPE (ASTM D3035 DR9, 250 PSI) low-pressure sewer (Respondents’ Exhibit A,
p. 5).
8. Under the Permit, the Project may provide sewer service for 31 single family homes
(Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 5).
9. The Permit requires privately owned simplex grinder pump sta(cid:415)ons to be installed on each
residen(cid:415)al property that will be serviced by the Project (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 5).
10. The Permit requires that the owners of each residen(cid:415)al property serviced by the Project
will be responsible for installing, providing power to, and maintaining the grinder pump
sta(cid:415)ons as well as the lateral service lines up to the connec(cid:415)on with the public sewer main
at the right-of-way line (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 5).
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 3 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

11. The Permit encompasses only the public por(cid:415)on of the low-pressure sanitary sewer
system (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 5).
12. Under the Permit, the Town is responsible for inspec(cid:415)ng the sewer installa(cid:415)on and for the
maintenance of public por(cid:415)on of the low-pressure sanitary sewer system a(cid:332)er the Project
is completed (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 5).
13. In addi(cid:415)on to imposing specific and general terms and condi(cid:415)ons, the Permit requires the
Project to conform to all provisions of 327 IAC 3 (Respondents’ Exhibit A, pp. 2-9).
14. The Permit may be modified, suspended, or revoked for cause including, but not limited
to, viola(cid:415)ons of any of the terms and/or condi(cid:415)ons and for misrepresenta(cid:415)on or failure
to fully disclose all relevant facts during the permi(cid:427)ng process (Respondents’ Exhibit A,
p. 6).
15. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner owns certain real property located on Page Road that may be affected by the
Permit and/or Project (Respondents’ Exhibit A, p. 17).
CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
1. This is a Final Order issued under Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-23. Findings of fact that may be
construed as conclusions of law and conclusions of law that may be construed as findings
of fact are so deemed.
2. The OALP has jurisdic(cid:415)on over and serves as the ul(cid:415)mate authority for administra(cid:415)ve
reviews of permits issued by the IDEM. See Indiana Code § 4-21.5, Ind. Code § 4-15-10.5-
12. In addi(cid:415)on, administra(cid:415)ve reviews of permits issued by the IDEM are governed by 315
IAC 1, et. seq.
3. Pursuant to Ind. Code § 4–21.5–3–14(c) “[a]t each stage of the proceeding, the agency or
other person requesting that an agency take action or asserting an affirmative defense
specified by law has the burden of persuasion and the burden of going forward with the
proof of the request or affirmative defense.” The party who has the burden of proof will
be required to prove their case by a preponderance of the evidence. Ind. Code § 4-21.5-
5-14, see also Huffman v. Office of Envtl. Adjud., 811 N.E.2d 806, 809 (Ind. 2004).
4. The ALJ must apply a de novo standard of review when determining the facts at issue.
Indiana Dept. of Natural Resources v. United Refuse Co., Inc., 615 N.E.2d 100 (Ind. 1993).
Findings of fact must be based exclusively on the evidence presented on the record and/or
ma(cid:425)ers that are officially no(cid:415)ced by the presiding ALJ - deference to the agency’s ini(cid:415)al
factual determina(cid:415)on is not allowed. Id.; Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27(d). Further, OALP is
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 4 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

required to base its findings of fact on substan(cid:415)al and reliable evidence. Ind. Code § 4-
21.5-3-27(d).
5. At any (cid:415)me a(cid:332)er the ALJ is assigned to the case, a party may move for summary judgment
in that party’s favor. Ind. Code § 4-21.5-23.
6. Pursuant to Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-23, an ALJ shall consider a summary judgment mo(cid:415)on
as would a court that is considering a mo(cid:415)on for summary judgment filed under Rule 56
of the Indiana Rules of Trial Procedure.
7. The ALJ may grant summary judgment if it finds that “the designated eviden(cid:415)ary ma(cid:425)er
shows that there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is
en(cid:415)tled to a judgment as a ma(cid:425)er of law.” Ind. Tr. R. 56(C); IC § 4-21.5-3-23.
8. “A fact is ‘material’ if its resolu(cid:415)on would affect the outcome of the case, and an issue is
‘genuine’ if a trier of fact is required to resolve the par(cid:415)es’ differing accounts of the truth
. . . or if the undisputed material facts support conflic(cid:415)ng reasonable inferences.” Williams
v. Tharp, 914 N.E.2d 756, 761 (Ind. 2009) (internal cita(cid:415)ons omi(cid:425)ed).
9. The moving party bears the burden of establishing that summary judgment is appropriate.
All facts and inferences must be construed in favor of the non-movant, and all doubts as
to the existence of a material issue must be resolved against the moving party. Gibson v.
Evansville Vanderburgh Building Commission, et al., 725 N.E.2d 949 (Ind. Ct. App. 2000);
City of North Vernon v. Jennings Northwest Regional U(cid:415)li(cid:415)es, 829 N.E.2d 1, (Ind. 2005);
Tibbs v. Huber, Hunt & Nichols, Inc., 668 N.E.2d 248, 249 (Ind. 1996).
10. A party opposing summary judgment must present specific facts demonstra(cid:415)ng a genuine
issue for trial. Hale v. Community Hospitals of Indianapolis, 567 N.E.2d 842, 843 (Ind. Ct.
App. 1991). When a mo(cid:415)on for summary judgment is made, an adverse party may not
rest upon the mere allega(cid:415)ons or denials of their pleading but must set forth specific facts
showing that there is a genuine issue for trial. Williams, 914 N.E.2d 756 (Ind. 2009).
11. Mere asser(cid:415)ons, opinions, or conclusions of law will not suffice to create a genuine issue
of material fact to preclude summary judgment. Sanchez v. Hamara, 534 N.E.2d 756, 758
(Ind. Ct. App. 1989), trans. denied; McMahan v. Snap-On Tool Corp., 478 N.E.2d 116, 122
(Ind. Ct. App. 1985).
12. The IDEM is a state agency that implements and enforces specified Indiana environmental
laws, and rules promulgated relevant to those laws, per Indiana Code § 13-13-1-1, et seq.
and Indiana Code § 13-14-1-1, et seq. These statutes also give the IDEM authority to
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 5 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

review and issue certain permits. See Ind. Code § 13-15-1, et. seq. The IDEM is authorized
to determine whether a permit should be issued by applying the relevant statutes and
regula(cid:415)ons pertaining to permits and can only consider said statutes and regula(cid:415)ons
when deciding whether to issue the permit. See American Suburban U(cid:415)li(cid:415)es, 2019 OEA
48, 53.
13. The Town is a municipality with powers, granted by the General Assembly, that are
necessary or desirable in the conduct of its affairs. See Ind. Code § 36-1-2-11; Ind. Code §
36-1-3-4. Specifically, the Town has explicit power to “acquire, construct, improve,
operate, and maintain sewage works.” See Ind. Code § 36-9-23-2. In an exercise of this
power, the Town submi(cid:425)ed an applica(cid:415)on to IDEM for a permit to construct a sanitary
sewer system along Page Road and Witmer Road.
14. Permits for the construc(cid:415)on of a sanitary sewer are required by and governed by the
requirements that are laid out 327 IAC 3. Administra(cid:415)ve review of a permit issued by the
IDEM is limited to whether IDEM acted in conformity with controlling statutes and
regula(cid:415)ons. See Aqua Indiana, Inc., 2010 OEA 168, ci(cid:415)ng In re: Objec(cid:415)on to Issuance of
Sec(cid:415)on 401 Water Quality Cer(cid:415)fica(cid:415)on COE ID No. 198800247 Conagra Soybean
Processing Co., 1998 WL 918585, at *3, OEA Cause No. 98-W-J-2052 (Nov. 12, 1988).
15. 315 IAC 1-3-2(b)(4)(A) requires a pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner in a case involving an administra(cid:415)ve appeal of
the issuance a permit to state with par(cid:415)cularity and iden(cid:415)fy:
(i) Environmental concerns or technical deficiencies related to the ac(cid:415)on of
the commissioner that is the subject of the pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on.
(ii) Permit terms and condi(cid:415)ons that the pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner contends would be
appropriate to comply with the law applicable to the contested permit.
16. Whenever a permit is required by any rule of the environmental rules board under Indiana
Code § 13-15-1 for the construc(cid:415)on, installa(cid:415)on, opera(cid:415)on, or modifica(cid:415)on of any facility,
equipment, or device, the permit may be issued only a(cid:332)er the IDEM has: (1) approved the
plans and specifica(cid:415)ons; and (2) determined that the facility, equipment, or device meets
the requirements of the applicable rule. Ind. Code § 13-15-3-5.
17. The undisputed facts in this ma(cid:425)er demonstrate that the IDEM reviewed and approved
the plans and specifica(cid:415)ons for the Project. The Town submi(cid:425)ed plans and specifica(cid:415)ons
to the IDEM during the permi(cid:427)ng process. Those plans and specifica(cid:415)ons - including the
design summary - were reviewed and approved by the IDEM through its issuance of the
Permit. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has failed to present any argument or evidence to the contrary.
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 6 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

18. The undisputed facts also demonstrate that Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has failed to allege, with the
required specificity, any way in which the Permit does not meet the requirements of the
applicable rule - 327 IAC 3. Specifically, neither the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on nor the
supplement/amendment thereto cite to any provision of 327 IAC 3 or to any specific
Permit term or condi(cid:415)on that the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner deems deficient under the law as required by
315 IAC 1-3-2. Further, neither the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on nor the supplement/amendment thereto
state, with par(cid:415)cularity, any environmental concern or technical defect related to IDEM’s
issuance of the Permit that stands in contraven(cid:415)on of 327 IAC 3 as required by 315 IAC 1-
3-2. Instead, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has alleged that the Town has not set forth evidence as to how
people without u(cid:415)lity service – par(cid:415)cularly the Amish property owners on Page Road -
will be able to install the required electric grinder pump sta(cid:415)ons, argued affected property
owners were not given informa(cid:415)on, and expressed various concerns related to the design
and future func(cid:415)onality of the Project should there be addi(cid:415)onal expansion.
19. It is important to note that under the applicable Indiana law, a pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for review of an
IDEM ac(cid:415)on must state with par(cid:415)cularity the issues proposed for considera(cid:415)on. See 315
IAC 1-3-2(a)(4); Ind. Code § 13-15-6-2(5). Issues not properly raised in the pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on are
waived. Bd. of Comm'rs of LaPorte Cnty. v. Great Lakes Transfer, LLC, 888 N.E.2d 784, 795
(Ind. Ct. App. 2008). As such, the issues raised by Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner in the summary judgment
proceedings that were not raised by the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on or the supplement/amendment thereto,
have been waived. However, even if the arguments had not been waived, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s
arguments fail nonetheless.
20. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s argument that the Town has not set forth evidence as to how people without
u(cid:415)lity service – par(cid:415)cularly the Amish property owners on Page Road - will be able to
install the required electric grinder pump sta(cid:415)ons is outside the scope of 327 IAC 3 and
fails to state a claim upon which relief may be granted. 327 IAC 3 does not require a
permi(cid:425)ee to show that future users of a sanitary sewer system have u(cid:415)lity power and/or
possess sufficient power to operate grinder pump sta(cid:415)ons (if required) for a construc(cid:415)on
permit to be issued. As such, the Town was not required to provide such evidence or
informa(cid:415)on nor was the IDEM authorized to require it as a condi(cid:415)on precedent to
approving the Town’s applica(cid:415)on and issuing the Permit. The only applicable requirement
contained within 327 IAC 3 related to grinder pumps states that an applicant must indicate
who will be responsible for maintaining the grinder pumps. See 327 IAC 3-2-2(e)(5); see
also Page Road, 2022 OEA 150, 154. The Town did precisely that when it noted in its
applica(cid:415)on that the grinder pumps would be privately owned and maintained.
21. Further, it is undisputed that the Permit at issue mandates compliance with its terms and
condi(cid:415)ons as well as 327 IAC 3. Under the Permit’s terms and condi(cid:415)ons, grinder pump
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 7 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

sta(cid:415)ons are required for each lateral line and/or property that seeks to connect to the
main sewer line. If a property owner does not have enough power to run a grinder pump
sta(cid:415)on as detailed in the Permit, that property cannot connect to the main line nor can it
send wastewater into the proposed sewer system. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s specula(cid:415)on that future
users may not have enough power to run the required pump sta(cid:415)ons is not a sufficient
basis for challenging or overturning the Permit. See Jennings, 909 N.E.2d at 1026. See also
DeGroot Dairy, 2006 OEA 1; Ge(cid:425)elfinger, 2005 OEA 1; Lafolle(cid:425)e Sta(cid:415)on Towne Centre,
2004 OEA 67; Grahn, 2004 OEA 40.
22. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s argument that poten(cid:415)ally affected property owners were not given certain
informa(cid:415)on fails to state a claim upon which relief can be granted. For a sewer permit, an
applicant must submit one prepared mailing label for each poten(cid:415)ally affected person for
IDEM to mail no(cid:415)ce of the permit when issued. See 327 IAC 3-2-2(e)(6). Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has
offered no evidence that IDEM did not comply with this requirement in issuing the Permit.
23. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner also takes issue with certain perceived discrepancies between the Town’s ini(cid:415)al
applica(cid:415)on submi(cid:425)ed on November 5, 2024, and the revised applica(cid:415)on submi(cid:425)ed on
February 3, 2025. The undisputed facts show that a(cid:332)er the submission of its ini(cid:415)al
applica(cid:415)on, the Town submi(cid:425)ed addi(cid:415)onal informa(cid:415)on and documenta(cid:415)on to IDEM and
that on February 3, 2025, it submi(cid:425)ed a revised applica(cid:415)on. Allega(cid:415)ons that fail to raise
any issue concerning compliance with controlling legal requirements fail to state a valid
claim or sufficient basis for challenging or overturning the Permit. Aqua Indiana, Inc.,
supra, ci(cid:415)ng In re: Objec(cid:415)ons to Issuance of Public Water Supply Construc(cid:415)on Permit No.
WS-2924.
24. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s concerns related to the design of the Project fail for the same reason. See Id.
First, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has failed to present any evidence or argument that the design of the
Project does not comply with 327 IAC 3. While Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner a(cid:425)empts to argue that IDEM’s
approval of 3-inch pipe in lieu of 4-inch pipe for the Project was somehow improper, his
argument finds no support in the undisputed facts or law. Specifically, 327 IAC 3-6-32 gives
the IDEM authority to approve alterna(cid:415)ve technical standards and the undisputed facts
demonstrate that is exactly what was done here. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has offered no evidence that
the IDEM should not have approved the 3-inch pipe or that the 3-inch pipe violates any of
the provisions under 327 IAC 3. Further, Indiana law does not authorize the IDEM to
dictate the design of a sanitary sewer beyond the requirements promulgated in 327 IAC
3. See Page Road, 2022 OEA 150.
25. Similarly, Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s concerns related to the future func(cid:415)onality of the Project should
there be an addi(cid:415)onal expansion also fails to state a valid claim or sufficient basis for
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-2502-000857
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 8 of 11
oalp@oalp.in.gov | 317-234-6689

challenging or overturning the Permit. The first of Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s concerns related to
func(cid:415)onality centers on his unsupported belief that the Project will not be able to
accommodate the an(cid:415)cipated flow from the 31 equivalent dwelling units (“EDU”) noted
in the Permit. The undisputed facts show that the Project will poten(cid:415)ally receive flow from
78 Equivalent Dwelling Units (EDUs). Id. pp. 46-47. The Town’s calcula(cid:415)ons show that the
3-inch pipe for this ini(cid:415)al sewer line project will not only be capable of handling flow from
the 31 EDUs stated in the updated applica(cid:415)on and Permit but from future, increased flows
as well. Id. pp. 4, 10, 46-47. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner has offered no evidence that the design flow
calcula(cid:415)ons are incorrect, that the approved system is insufficiently sized, or that IDEM’s
approval violates any provision under 327 IAC 3.
26. Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner’s second concern related to the future func(cid:415)onality of the Project is predicated
on his unsupported belief that that the Town has authority under Ind. Code § 36-9-23-30
to force, and will force, certain users to connect to the Project and will therefore
necessitate an addi(cid:415)onal expansion of the Project in upwards of ten to twenty years from
now. But whether the Town may have the authority under Ind. Code § 36-9-23-30.1 to
force connec(cid:415)ons to the Project has no relevance to IDEM’s issuance of the Permit. IDEM
approved the Permit under 327 IAC 3 based on the proposed design submi(cid:425)ed by the
Town for the Project. Should an expansion be required in the future, a new permit will
need to be obtained and meet the requirements of 327 IAC 3. Again, allega(cid:415)ons that fail
to raise any issue concerning compliance with controlling legal requirements fail to state
a valid claim. Aqua Indiana, Inc., supra, ci(cid:415)ng In re: Objec(cid:415)ons to Issuance of Public Water
Supply Construc(cid:415)on Permit No. WS-2924.
